issue.title: Exact-artifact-delta prep still shallow-copies the full Agents roster instead of the affected closure
issue.description:
Epic sase-1t3.13.1 (phase sase-1t3.13.1.4, commit 10922458c1) added an exact-artifact-delta
fast path. It replaced the deep `copy_agent_graph` detach with
`copy_agent_rows_delta_isolated`, then shares untouched rows back after the pipeline. The
retained objects are now delta-sized, but the transient copy still covers the full roster.
`own_exact_delta_snapshot_fast` (src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_loading_graph.py)
shallow-copies every cached, capacity, and fleet row. It also detaches every mutable
container on every copy before the merge, slot, tree, and finalize pipeline runs.

The epic plan required the opposite for representative small deltas: "copying must scale
with the affected closure, not the full roster". Integration phase sase-1t3.13.1.5 measured
2- and 8-row deltas on 150- and 600-row graphs. Shallow Agent copies were 150/150/600/600,
while only 2/8/2/8 changed rows stayed new after share-back. The land agent's probe (Agent
has 317 dataclass fields) measured worker prep of about 37 ms at 165 rows and about 175 ms
at 660 rows for a 2- or 8-row delta. Pure-Python copy work on a worker thread still competes
with the event loop for the GIL. The copies also carry container/member reference cycles,
so each delta leaves cyclic garbage for the GC.

Root cause: the whole-roster passes write to rows the delta did not touch. These include
relationship normalization in _loading_compute_merge, runner-slot annotation
(refresh_runner_slot_context), named-proc carryover, clan/fold/fleet projection, and
finalize. That forces whole-roster isolation. Baseline phase sase-1t3.13.1.1 also showed
that a naive closure copy does not bound the cost, because clan `runtime_children` fans out
to every member through the shared memo.

Remediation needs a scoped normalizer. Classify the delta (EXACT_DELTA_RELATIONSHIP_KEYS
in _loading_compute_merge.py already documents the scalar-vs-structural boundary). Copy
only the rows a scalar delta's passes actually write, normalize only the owned affected
component, and splice it into a new roster sequence. Broad or structural deltas fall back
with an explicit trace reason. Audit every pass for in-place writes to unowned rows first.

Not caused by the epic: before the epic, every exact delta deep-copied the full roster,
which was about 16x more expensive. The epic reduced the cost but did not reach the plan's
target. The land agent recorded this miss rather than block the epic's closure.

task_type_fields.impact: Every exact artifact delta (the common running-agent refresh path) allocates and cycle-collects O(roster) Agent copies off-thread: about 175 ms of worker CPU at 660 rows. That contends for the GIL with the TUI event loop and adds heap churn the sase-1t3 heap-recovery work is trying to remove.
task_type_fields.repro: Build 150- and 600-row normalized rosters (tests/_agents_tab_graph_isolation_helpers.normalize_agent_graph plus make_agent). Wrap them with incomplete_tier1_snapshot(load_state=delta_load_state()) and feed 2 or 8 status-changed incoming rows to prepare_loaded_agents_worker_boundary. Count copy_agent_rows_delta_isolated outputs: it is one copy per roster row (150/600), not per affected row.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1t3.13.1's integration phase measured that exact-delta preparation still allocates one shallow copy per roster row for 2- and 8-row deltas, missing the epic plan's 'copy scales with affected closure' target. The land agent confirmed the miss predates the epic and recorded it as a follow-up instead of blocking closure.
